methodological_rigor.justification: This is a 3-year follow-up (secondary analysis) of RATIONALE-309, a double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter phase 3 RCT in 42 Asian sites (N=263) with IRC-assessed PFS primary endpoint, stratified randomization (sex, liver metastasis), and prespecified statistical analysis plan. Crossover is handled with both RPSFTM and 2-stage methods to address 52.3% crossover. Exploratory biomarker analyses use prespecified GEP signatures. Limitations (Asian-only, crossover, subgroup interpretation) are explicitly acknowledged.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Tislelizumab plus chemotherapy is approved by both the European Commission and Chinese NMPA for first-line recurrent/metastatic NPC; this 3-year follow-up provides mature OS data (HR 0.73; median 45.3 vs 31.8 months) that directly supports ongoing regulatory and guideline recommendations. Exploratory B-cell signature biomarker adds potential for biomarker-guided therapy. Individual phase 3 RCT -> Oxford LoE 1b.

reporting_quality.justification: Authors explicitly state CONSORT adherence and publish protocol (Supplement 1), SAP (Supplement 2), and eMethods (Supplement 3). Patient-disposition figure, AE grading per CTCAE v5.0, and detailed statistical methods are provided. Registration (NCT03924986) and IRB approvals documented. Data availability statement is not visible in the normalized text (likely in online content).

novelty_literature.justification: This is a mature follow-up of a previously reported trial (interim published in Cancer Cell 2023), extending findings to 3-year OS, crossover-adjusted analyses, and confirmatory biomarker analyses. Findings are consistent with prior interim data and with JUPITER-02 and CAPTAIN-1st, so novelty lies mainly in OS maturity and B-cell biomarker refinement rather than new therapeutic class or mechanism. Incremental but clinically important extension.

writing_presentation.justification: Clear JAMA-style writing with structured abstract, explicit primary/secondary analyses, and thorough discussion benchmarking against JUPITER-02 and CAPTAIN-1st. Figures and tables are well described, and limitations are candid about the Asian-only population and crossover caveats. Biomarker discussion is nuanced and appropriately speculative.

key_strengths: Mature 3-year OS data from a double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 RCT in a disease with limited options
Clinically meaningful median OS improvement (45.3 vs 31.8 months; HR 0.73) despite 52.3% crossover
RPSFTM (HR 0.56) and 2-stage crossover-adjusted analyses (HR 0.62) consistent with primary result
Exploratory B-cell signature biomarker (OS HR 0.41 in high expressors) extends mechanistic insight
Safety profile consistent with the class, manageable immune-mediated AEs
key_concerns: Enrolled exclusively in Asia; generalizability to keratinizing NPC populations limited
Secondary analysis of a previously published pivotal trial; OS HR CI crosses 1.0 in primary analysis
Biomarker findings exploratory and require prospective validation
Data availability statement not visible in normalized text
chief_reviewer.rationale: Long-term follow-up of a pivotal RCT supporting current approvals with mature OS and biomarker insights; fits top-tier oncology journals (JAMA Oncology/Lancet Oncology/JCO class) with minor revisions to clarify data availability and biomarker caveats.
